reforms.description: The federal government proposed expansion of math-science education research funding, allocating $100-200 million in 1994 as part of a broader human capital and education initiative.
reforms.package_name: 1994 Education and Human Capital Budget Package
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in math-science research and education builds human capital and scientific capacity, which are foundational to long-term productivity growth and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'math-science education research ($100-200 million in 1994)' as a proposed funding increase in the budget package, but notes that 'the appropriations process is ongoing, so actual spending levels may change.'
reforms.importance_rationale: This is a modest, targeted research funding initiative within a broader education package. While it supports an important area (STEM research and education), the allocation is relatively small and incremental rather than structural.

reforms.description: The new Administration redirected federal R&D spending away from defence-related research toward civilian and dual-use technologies by reforming national laboratories and the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, and mandating increased R&D cooperation with industry through CRADAs (cooperative research and development agreements).
reforms.component_name: Reorientation of federal R&D from defence to civilian and dual-use technologies
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Redirecting R&D from defence to civilian applications increases spillovers to commercial sectors and improves productivity growth. CRADAs strengthen knowledge transfer between public research institutions and private firms.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'Henceforth, federally-funded mission-oriented R&D will be used to try to improve the productivity of private R&D. Accordingly, the share of purely military R&D is being cut back, and resources are being directed to civilian and dual-use technologies.'
reforms.importance_rationale: This represents a structural reorientation of U.S. federal R&D policy, shifting the allocation of nearly $70 billion in annual federal R&D spending away from defence (which represented 29% of total R&D) toward civilian applications. The reform affects multiple federal agencies and establishes a new governance framework (CRADAs) for public-private collaboration, with over 1,500 agreements valued at $323 million already in place by 1992.
reforms.source_quote: Henceforth, federally-funded mission-oriented R&D will be used to try to improve the productivity of private R&D. Accordingly, the share of purely military R&D is being cut back, and resources are being directed to civilian and dual-use technologies by reforming existing agencies (national laboratories and the former Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency).

reforms.description: The new Administration proposed a major budgetary increase of $535 million in FY 1994 (nearly double the prior year's allocation) for the National Institute of Standards and Technology to expand its Advanced Technology Program, which develops high-risk generic pre-commercial and pre-competitive technologies with partial private-sector funding.
reforms.component_name: Advanced Technology Program expansion at NIST
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Public funding for pre-competitive generic R&D addresses market failures where social returns exceed private returns, stimulating private R&D efforts and generating significant spillovers to the broader economy.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'The new Administration has also indicated a willingness to move toward greater activism by proposing a major budgetary increase ($535 million in FY 1994, nearly double this year's allocation) for the National Institute of Standards and Technology.'
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant expansion of an existing programme (NIST's Advanced Technology Program) with substantial budgetary increase (nearly 100% increase), targeting pre-competitive generic technologies where market failures justify public intervention. The reform reflects a shift toward greater government activism in technology policy.
reforms.source_quote: The new Administration has also indicated a willingness to move toward greater activism by proposing a major budgetary increase ($535 million in FY 1994, nearly double this year's allocation) for the National Institute of Standards and Technology to proceed with its Advanced Technology Program to develop high-risk generic technologies.

reforms.description: The Administration proposed to make the Research and Experimentation tax credit (established in 1981) permanent, which would enhance its effectiveness in incentivizing private R&D spending. The credit had been extended and modified multiple times, with its temporary nature criticized for biasing firms away from long-term projects.
reforms.component_name: Permanence of Research and Experimentation tax credit
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Making the tax credit permanent reduces uncertainty and encourages long-term R&D investment by firms. Recent analysis shows substantial elasticity of R&D spending to tax incentives, with spillovers generating social returns exceeding private returns.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'The Administration proposed to make the credit permanent which would have served to enhance its effectiveness, but Congress extended it only through June 1995.'
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant reform to an existing major tax instrument (equivalent to over $1.5 billion per year in government expenditure). Making the credit permanent would address a key criticism regarding its temporary nature and improve incentives for long-term R&D projects, though the proposal was not fully adopted by Congress.
reforms.source_quote: The Administration proposed to make the credit permanent which would have served to enhance its effectiveness, but Congress extended it only through June 1995. Others have suggested that it should be made available to commercialisation expenditures as well.

reforms.description: The Administration intends to promote 'Regional Technology Alliances' and 'Agile Manufacturing Programs' to exploit network externalities and support R&D consortia to overcome non-appropriability problems, avoid duplication, and speed technology diffusion throughout industries.
reforms.component_name: Regional Technology Alliances and Agile Manufacturing Programs
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D consortia can enhance productivity by overcoming non-appropriability and exploiting scale economies, but carry antitrust risks and may favor large visible projects over smaller promising ones, creating potential inefficiencies.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'The Administration intends to promote' these programmes, indicating announcement without clear evidence of legislation or implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant initiative to support collaborative R&D and technology diffusion through regional alliances and manufacturing programs, addressing market failures in knowledge spillovers and network externalities.
reforms.source_quote: The Administration intends to promote 'Regional Technology Alliances' and 'Agile Manufacturing Programs' in order to assist in the exploitation of network externalities, and technology outreach or extension centres to stimulate technology transfer and ensure diffusion of innovations.

reforms.description: The Administration will establish technology outreach or extension centres to stimulate technology transfer and ensure diffusion of innovations across industries, supporting knowledge dissemination from research to practitioners.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Extension centres reduce barriers to technology adoption and diffusion, enabling firms to access and implement research-based innovations, thereby raising productivity and allocative efficiency.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states the Administration 'will also increase the emphasis on joint ventures' and establish extension centres, indicating announcement of intent.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted initiative to address technology diffusion and the 'not-invented-here' syndrome, supporting adoption of innovations across industries through extension services.
reforms.source_quote: technology outreach or extension centres to stimulate technology transfer and ensure diffusion of innovations

reforms.description: The government will provide funding for pilot projects in education and health-care spheres and $784 million over four years for 'cross-cutting high performance computing' as part of establishing a national information infrastructure.
reforms.component_name: High Performance Computing and Information Infrastructure
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in high-performance computing infrastructure and information networks enhances research capacity and enables knowledge creation and diffusion, supporting long-term productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states the government 'will provide funding' for pilot projects and computing infrastructure, indicating announced policy.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant infrastructure investment supporting research and innovation through high-performance computing and information networks, with applications across education and health sectors.
reforms.source_quote: $784 million over the next four years for related 'cross-cutting high performance computing'

reforms.description: The automobile industry will receive targeted government assistance to develop technologies enhancing environmental friendliness of vehicle use, supporting sectoral R&D in clean vehicle technology.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted R&D support for environmental vehicle technologies can enhance competitiveness in emerging markets and reduce long-term compliance costs while supporting innovation in a major industrial sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'the automobile industry will benefit from targeted assistance with a view to developing technologies', indicating announced policy.
reforms.importance_rationale: A narrowly targeted sectoral initiative supporting R&D in environmental vehicle technologies, representing incremental support for a specific industry rather than system-wide change.
reforms.source_quote: the automobile industry will benefit from targeted assistance with a view to developing technologies to enhance environmental friendliness of vehicle use

reforms.description: The government will provide support for the development of new equipment and software to facilitate education in both formal and informal settings, supporting educational technology innovation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in educational technology can enhance human capital formation and skill development, supporting long-term productivity growth and workforce competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'support will be given to the development of new equipment and software', indicating announced policy.
reforms.importance_rationale: A narrowly targeted initiative supporting development of educational technology tools. While relevant to human capital, it does not fit cleanly into standard innovation policy categories as it focuses on educational tools rather than research infrastructure or human capital for research.
reforms.source_quote: support will be given to the development of new equipment and software to facilitate education in both formal and informal settings

reforms.description: The Administration proposed energy research and conservation spending as part of its broader investment package, allocating funds to support research and development in energy technologies and conservation methods.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Energy R&D and conservation investments build technological capacity and reduce long-term energy costs, supporting productivity and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform was included in OBRA93, which was passed into law in 1993 and began implementation in 1994.
reforms.importance_rationale: Energy R&D is a significant sectoral investment within a major deficit-reduction and investment package, but the text does not specify the exact allocation or scope of energy research funding, limiting assessment of its structural importance.
reforms.source_quote: Substantial amounts are to be made available for transportation infrastructure... environmental protection, rural development, energy research and conservation...

reforms.description: The text discusses the temporary extension of the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit, which provides tax incentives for firms conducting R&D. New rules confine its availability to domestic research, intended to induce marginal increases in equipment investment to incorporate R&D output.
reforms.component_name: Research and Experimentation Tax Credit Extension
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits reduce the cost of innovation investment for firms, incentivizing private-sector research spending and embodiment of R&D outputs in capital equipment, which can raise productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'The temporary extension of the Research and Experimentation Tax credit (see below) and new rules confining its availability to domestic research may induce a marginal increase in equipment investment' in the context of the 1994 Budget.
reforms.importance_rationale: A marginal extension of an existing tax credit instrument with modest expected effects on investment. While innovation-relevant, it is narrowly scoped and incremental rather than structural.
reforms.source_quote: The temporary extension of the Research and Experimentation Tax credit (see below) and new rules confining its availability to domestic research may induce a marginal increase in equipment investment to incorporate the R&D output, a few years hence.

reforms.description: The Administration proposed the Defence Reinvestment and Conversion Initiative, a $20 billion package over five years (rising to $5.2 billion in FY 1997) designed to redirect federal R&D away from defence towards civilian applications. The initiative includes 29 programmes, with a focus on partnerships between industry and 726 national laboratories for dual-use technology development and matching grants for industry-led R&D.
reforms.component_name: National laboratories partnerships and dual-use R&D matching grants
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Redirects substantial public R&D resources from defence to civilian applications, potentially improving allocative efficiency and private-sector innovation capacity through knowledge transfer and collaborative research.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'For fiscal 1993 it includes $1.4 billion appropriated by Congress last year, but not spent, plus another $0.3 billion,' indicating the programme was in effect during the 1993 fiscal year.
reforms.importance_rationale: This is a major structural reform redirecting a significant portion of federal R&D spending ($20 billion over five years) from defence to civilian applications. It represents a system-wide reorientation of national R&D priorities and involves substantial institutional partnerships across 726 national laboratories and private industry, with lasting implications for the innovation ecosystem.
reforms.source_quote: The Administration has proposed the Defence Reinvestment and Conversion Initiative to ease the transition. It embodies 29 different programmes... there are a series which will try to set up partnerships between industry and the 726 national laboratories (that do some $23 billion or about 13 per cent of the nation's total R&D), especially for dual-use technology, and provide matching grants for industry-led R&D.

reforms.description: The Administration proposed permanent extension of the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit to increase its efficiency by reducing uncertainty, while cautioning against making it more generous since not all R&D output is inappropriable.
reforms.component_name: Research and Experimentation Tax Credit Extension
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Permanent extension reduces uncertainty for private R&D investment, lowering the cost of capital for innovation and encouraging sustained private-sector research spending.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Permanent extension of the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit would have increased its efficiency by reducing uncertainty' — phrased as a proposal, not implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant but targeted instrument reform affecting private R&D incentives. Permanent extension would reduce policy uncertainty and improve efficiency of an existing tax instrument, with meaningful but not system-wide impact.
reforms.source_quote: Permanent extension of the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit would have increased its efficiency by reducing uncertainty, but it should probably not be made more generous, since not all R&D output is inappropriable.

reforms.description: The Administration proposed greater federal involvement in pre-competitive generic R&D, contingent on substantial private-sector financial participation and careful avoidance of political influence in project selection and location decisions.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Public funding of pre-competitive generic R&D addresses market failure in basic research with positive spillovers; private co-financing ensures relevance and cost-sharing discipline.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Greater federal involvement in pre-competitive generic R&D is legitimate, so long as there is substantial private-sector financial participation' — framed as a policy position, not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant policy shift toward public-private R&D collaboration in basic research, addressing market failure in generic technology development. Meaningful but conditional on governance safeguards.
reforms.source_quote: Greater federal involvement in pre-competitive generic R&D is legitimate, so long as there is substantial private-sector financial participation and care is taken to avoid political influence in project selection and location decisions.

reforms.description: The Administration proposed setting up technology outreach or extension centres to alleviate problems of exploiting and diffusing existing technology.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Technology extension centres reduce barriers to technology adoption and diffusion, raising productivity by helping firms access and implement existing innovations.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'The problems of exploiting and diffusing existing technology could be alleviated by the proposed setting-up of technology outreach or extension centres' — framed as a proposal.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted but potentially broad-reaching initiative to improve technology diffusion and adoption across the economy. Addresses a real market failure in technology transfer but is narrower than system-wide infrastructure reform.
reforms.source_quote: The problems of exploiting and diffusing existing technology could be alleviated by the proposed setting-up of technology outreach or extension centres.

reforms.description: The Administration proposed closer cooperation between national laboratories and private industry to shift federal R&D spending from defence-related projects toward civilian and dual-use technologies.
reforms.component_name: National Laboratories-Industry Cooperation and Civilian R&D Shift
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Redirecting R&D from defence to civilian and dual-use technologies increases commercial spillovers and productivity growth; closer lab-industry cooperation accelerates technology transfer and commercialisation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'direct federal outlays are set to shift to civilian and dual-use technologies. Also worthwhile is the closer co-operation between the national laboratories and private industry' — framed as Administration policy direction.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant reorientation of national laboratory R&D toward civilian applications and private-sector collaboration. Reflects a structural shift in R&D priorities but implementation depends on budget allocation decisions.
reforms.source_quote: To this point too much of the nation's R&D spending has been devoted to defence-related projects, and direct federal outlays are set to shift to civilian and dual-use technologies. Also worthwhile is the closer co-operation between the national laboratories and private industry.

reforms.description: The 1984 National Co-operative Research Act eliminated private antitrust risks for R&D joint ventures, enabling rivals to collaborate on research while competing on production. Over 300 R&D joint ventures have been registered under the Act, with concentration in information technology, biotechnology and new materials.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Reduces legal barriers to private R&D collaboration, enabling firms to pool resources and share knowledge in pre-competitive research, which increases innovation efficiency and reduces duplication.
reforms.status_evidence: Over 300 R&D joint ventures have been registered under the Act, with concentration in information technology, biotechnology and new materials.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural reform eliminating antitrust barriers to private R&D collaboration. Enabled a new governance model for pre-competitive research across multiple sectors, with sustained uptake (300+ ventures registered by 1993). Addresses a fundamental market failure in knowledge creation.
reforms.source_quote: These are purely social risks, as the private risks of triple damages were eliminated by the 1984 National Co-operative Research Act. After a slow start, the latest count shows that over 300 R&D joint ventures have been registered under the Act, with concentration in information technology, biotechnology and new materials.

reforms.description: Sematech, a $200 million semiconductor R&D joint venture launched in 1987, was funded jointly by the semiconductor industry and the Department of Defence. Its major success has been to improve communications between its chip-making members and equipment producers.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Public-private R&D consortium in semiconductors addresses coordination failures between chip makers and equipment producers, improving industry-wide technological capability and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: Sematech was launched in 1987 and funded jointly by the industry and the Department of Defence. Its major success has been to improve communications between its chip-making members and equipment producers.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D initiative combining public and private funding in a strategically important industry (semiconductors). Demonstrates a model for addressing coordination failures in pre-competitive research, though narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: The most publicised case is that of the $200 million Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology (Sematech), launched in 1987 and funded jointly by the industry and the Department of Defence. Its major success has been to improve communications between its chip-making members and equipment producers.
